sn.e: At the bottom right there is a box with a QR code.
That box is the most important part.
Everything is in the box.

sn.s: Das Konto, der Betrag, der Name.
sn.e: The account, the amount, the name.
You do not have to type anything in.

sn.s: Es gibt drei Wege zum Zahlen.
sn.e: There are three ways to pay.

sn.s: Der erste Weg ist das Handy.
sn.e: The first way is your phone.
You open the app.

sn.s: Man hält das Handy über den Code.
sn.e: You hold the phone over the code.
Then everything is already there.

sn.s: Man drückt einmal und es ist bezahlt.
sn.e: You press once and it is paid.

sn.s: Der zweite Weg ist der Automat.
sn.e: The second way is the machine.

sn.s: Bei der Post steht ein Automat.
sn.e: There is a machine at the post office.
You put the bill in.
The machine reads the code.

sn.s: Dann zahlt man mit der Karte.
sn.e: Then you pay with your card.

sn.s: Der dritte Weg ist der Schalter.
sn.e: The third way is the counter.

sn.s: Man geht auf die Post und stellt sich an.
sn.e: You go to the post office and queue.

sn.s: Man legt die Rechnung auf den Schalter.
sn.e: You put the bill on the counter.
You can pay in cash.
That is the most expensive way.
You pay two francs extra.

sn.s: Aber viele Leute machen es trotzdem.
sn.e: But a lot of people do it anyway.

sn.s: Ich habe die App auf dem Handy.
sn.e: I have the app on my phone.

sn.s: Ich mache sie auf und schaue sie an.
sn.e: I open it and look at it.
I close it again.
I do not trust it yet.

sn.s: Ich verstehe nicht jedes Wort darin.
sn.e: I do not understand every word in it.

sn.s: Und es geht um viel Geld.
sn.e: And it is about a lot of money.

sn.s: Also gehe ich auf die Post.
sn.e: So I go to the post office.

sn.s: Ich nehme alle vier Rechnungen mit.
sn.e: I take all four bills with me.

sn.s: Ich stelle mich in die Reihe.
sn.e: I join the queue.

sn.s: Vor mir steht wieder ein alter Mann.
sn.e: In front of me there is an old man again.
Maybe it is the same one.
He is paying his bills too.

sn.s: Jetzt stehe ich neben ihm in der gleichen Reihe.
sn.e: Now I am standing next to him in the same queue.

sn.s: Das finde ich komisch und auch gut.
sn.e: I find that odd and also good.
It is my turn.

sn.s: Die Frau nimmt die vier Rechnungen.
sn.e: The woman takes the four bills.

sn.s: Sie liest jeden Code mit einem Gerät.
sn.e: She reads each code with a device.
It beeps four times.
She says the total.
Five hundred and twelve francs.
I pay with the card.
She gives me four receipts.

sn.s: Ich lege sie in die Mappe.
sn.e: I put them in the folder.

sn.s: Alles ist bezahlt und ich habe es auf Papier.
sn.e: Everything is paid and I have it on paper.
That is a good feeling.
Nuno laughs at me.

sn.s: Er sagt: Du zahlst am Schalter?
sn.e: He says: you pay at the counter?

sn.s: Er sagt: Das machen nur alte Leute.
sn.e: He says: only old people do that.
I say: I know.

sn.s: Ich sage: Nächsten Monat mache ich es mit dem Handy.
sn.e: I say: next month I will do it with my phone.
He says: so you say.
He is right.

sn.s: Ich gehe noch zweimal auf die Post.
sn.e: I go to the post office twice more.

sn.s: Erst im dritten Monat nehme ich das Handy.
sn.e: Only in the third month do I use my phone.

sn.s: Dann geht es in zehn Sekunden.
sn.e: Then it takes ten seconds.

sn.s: Und ich frage mich, warum ich so lange warte.
sn.e: And I wonder why I waited so long.

sn.s: Eine Rechnung darf man nicht vergessen.
sn.e: You must not forget a bill.

sn.s: Nach der Frist kommt eine Mahnung.
sn.e: After the deadline a reminder comes.
Nobody wants a reminder.

sn.s: Nach der zweiten Mahnung wird es ernst.
sn.e: After the second reminder it gets serious.
A reminder costs twenty francs.
The second reminder costs more.

sn.s: Und danach wird es richtig teuer.
sn.e: And after that it gets seriously expensive.

sn.s: Frau Amrein sagt: Zahlen Sie immer sofort.
sn.e: Frau Amrein says: always pay straight away.

sn.s: Sie sagt: Legen Sie eine Rechnung nie weg.
sn.e: She says: never put a bill aside.

sn.s: Sie zahlt alles am gleichen Tag.
sn.e: She pays everything the same day.
The same day, always.

sn.s: Ich mache es jetzt auch so.
sn.e: I do it that way now too.

sn.s: Die Rechnung kommt und ich zahle sie.
sn.e: The bill comes and I pay it.

sn.s: Dann liegt sie in der Mappe und ist fertig.
sn.e: Then it lies in the folder and it is done.
That is easier than waiting.
And I sleep better.

lessons.title: Fasnacht
lessons.desc: You wake at five to brass instruments deliberately playing wrong

sn.s: Im Februar wird die Stadt anders.
sn.e: In February the town changes.
There are masks hanging in the shops.
There are pictures in the windows.
Everywhere there is one word: Fasnacht.
I ask Frau Amrein about it.

sn.s: Sie sagt nur: Schlafen Sie gut am Mittwoch.
sn.e: She says only: sleep well on Wednesday.
She explains nothing more.
I only understand why later.

sn.s: Am Donnerstag um fünf Uhr wache ich auf.
sn.e: On Thursday at five o'clock I wake up.
Outside it is dark.
Outside it is very loud.
I hear drums.

sn.s: Eine Trommel hört man durch alles.
sn.e: You hear a drum through everything.

sn.s: Die Trommel gibt den Takt und der Rest folgt.
sn.e: The drum sets the beat and the rest follows.
I hear music.
The music is wrong.
The notes are wrong.

sn.s: Sie sind alle ein bisschen daneben.
sn.e: They are all a little off.

sn.s: Ich denke zuerst: die können nicht spielen.
sn.e: At first I think: they cannot play.
That is a mistake.
They play wrong on purpose.
That is the whole point.
I go to the window.

sn.s: Auf der Strasse gehen hundert Leute.
sn.e: There are a hundred people in the street.
Everybody is in costume.

sn.s: Verkleiden heisst: man zieht etwas anderes an.
sn.e: Verkleiden means: you put something else on.
You are somebody else.

sn.s: Sie haben Masken auf dem Gesicht.
sn.e: They have masks on their faces.

sn.s: Die Masken sind gross und hässlich und schön.
sn.e: The masks are big and ugly and beautiful.

sn.s: Sie haben Instrumente in den Händen.
sn.e: They have instruments in their hands.
Drums, trumpets, big horns.
And they all play wrong together.

sn.s: Es ist fünf Uhr am Morgen.
sn.e: It is five in the morning.
I think about the quiet hours.

sn.s: Ich denke an das Klopfen an der Decke.
sn.e: I think about the knocking on the ceiling.
I think about the Hausordnung.

sn.s: Und ich verstehe gar nichts mehr.
sn.e: And I understand nothing at all any more.

sn.s: Das ganze Jahr ist es still.
sn.e: All year it is quiet.

sn.s: Man darf nicht duschen und nicht waschen.
sn.e: You may not shower and not do laundry.

sn.s: Und dann ist es um fünf Uhr so laut.
sn.e: And then at five o'clock it is this loud.

sn.s: Ich ziehe mich an und gehe hinunter.
sn.e: I get dressed and go down.

sn.s: Auf der Strasse ist die halbe Stadt.
sn.e: Half the town is in the street.
Old people, children, everybody.

sn.s: Um fünf Uhr am Morgen im Februar.
sn.e: At five in the morning in February.

sn.s: Es ist kalt und alle sind draussen.
sn.e: It is cold and everybody is outside.

sn.s: Ich sehe Herrn Bucher von unten.
sn.e: I see Herr Bucher from downstairs.
He is wearing a mask.
He is playing a drum.

sn.s: Der Mann mit dem Klopfen an der Decke.
sn.e: The man with the knocking on the ceiling.
He sees me and laughs.
He shouts: Fasnacht!
That explains everything and nothing.
The Fasnacht lasts six days.

sn.s: Die Fasnacht ist im Februar oder im März.
sn.e: The Fasnacht is in February or March.

sn.s: Fasnacht macht die halbe Stadt mit.
sn.e: Half the town joins in the Fasnacht.
From Thursday to Tuesday.
Six days of noise and music.

sn.s: Am Mittwoch ist es plötzlich fertig.
sn.e: On Wednesday it is suddenly over.

sn.s: Am Mittwoch ist die Stadt wieder still.
sn.e: On Wednesday the town is quiet again.
Completely quiet, like before.

sn.s: Am Donnerstag gehe ich zur Arbeit.
sn.e: On Thursday I go to work.

sn.s: Ich bin müde und ich habe keine Idee.
sn.e: I am tired and I have no idea.

sn.s: Vielleicht habe ich frei und vielleicht nicht.
sn.e: Maybe I have the day off and maybe not.

sn.s: Halb Luzern hat frei und halb nicht.
sn.e: Half of Luzern has the day off and half does not.

sn.s: Am Abend gehe ich wieder auf die Strasse.
sn.e: In the evening I go out into the street again.

sn.s: Die Gruppen spielen an jeder Ecke.
sn.e: The groups play on every corner.
A group is called a Guggenmusik.
Every Guggenmusik has its own masks.

sn.s: Und ein eigenes Thema jedes Jahr.
sn.e: And its own theme every year.

sn.s: Sie üben das ganze Jahr dafür.
sn.e: They practise all year for it.
They practise playing wrong.
That takes some understanding.

sn.s: Ich stehe an einer Ecke und höre zu.
sn.e: I stand on a corner and listen.

sn.s: Nach zwei Stunden gefällt es mir.
sn.e: After two hours I like it.

sn.s: Es ist laut und es ist zu viel.
sn.e: It is loud and it is too much.

sn.s: Aber alle sind da und alle tanzen.
sn.e: But everybody is there and everybody dances.

sn.s: Auch die stillsten Leute im Haus.
sn.e: Even the quietest people in the building.
Ruedi Zemp is standing next to me.

sn.s: Er sagt zum ersten Mal einen ganzen Satz.
sn.e: For the first time he says a whole sentence.

sn.s: Er sagt: Sechs Tage im Jahr sind wir anders.
sn.e: He says: six days a year we are different.
Then he is silent again.

sn.s: Das ist der längste Satz von ihm bis jetzt.
sn.e: That is the longest sentence from him so far.

sn.s: Am Dienstagabend ist der letzte Abend.
sn.e: Tuesday evening is the last evening.

sn.s: Die Musik hört um Mitternacht auf.
sn.e: The music stops at midnight.
Not slowly. All at once.
At midnight it is quiet.
The people go home.

sn.s: Am Mittwochmorgen putzen alle die Strasse.
sn.e: On Wednesday morning everybody cleans the street.

sn.s: Um sieben Uhr ist die Stadt wieder sauber.
sn.e: By seven the town is clean again.

sn.s: Kein Papier mehr auf dem Boden.
sn.e: No more paper on the ground.
That surprises me most.

sn.s: Sechs Tage Chaos und dann alles wieder in Ordnung.
sn.e: Six days of chaos and then everything back in order.
The two things go together.

sn.s: Vielleicht geht das eine nur mit dem anderen.
sn.e: Maybe one only works with the other.

lessons.title: Falsch getrennt
lessons.desc: She shows you what you did and then gives you soup

sn.s: Am Dienstag klopft es an meiner Tür.
sn.e: On Tuesday there is a knock at my door.

sn.s: Vor der Tür steht Frau Amrein.
sn.e: Frau Amrein is outside the door.

sn.s: Sie hat meinen Sack in der Hand.
sn.e: She has my bag in her hand.
My PET bag.

sn.s: Sie sagt: Haben Sie eine Minute?
sn.e: She says: do you have a minute?
That is never a question.

sn.s: Wir gehen zusammen in die Küche.
sn.e: We go into the kitchen together.

sn.s: Sie stellt den Sack auf den Tisch.
sn.e: She puts the bag on the table.
She opens it.
She takes three things out.
She lays them side by side.
The first is a milk bottle.

sn.s: Sie sagt: Das ist kein PET.
sn.e: She says: that is not PET.

sn.s: Ich sage: Aber es ist eine Flasche.
sn.e: I say: but it is a bottle.
She turns the bottle over.
There is a small symbol on the bottom.

sn.s: Bei PET steht PET, sagt sie.
sn.e: On PET it says PET, she says.
On milk it says something else.

sn.s: Die Milchflasche kommt in den Kehricht.
sn.e: The milk bottle goes in the rubbish.

sn.s: Oder in den Laden, in einen anderen Container.
sn.e: Or to the shop, in a different container.
The second is a lid.
A lid from a bottle.

sn.s: Sie sagt: Der Deckel bleibt auf der Flasche.
sn.e: She says: the lid stays on the bottle.

sn.s: Ich sage: Ich denke, man muss ihn abmachen.
sn.e: I say: I thought you had to take it off.

sn.s: Sie sagt: Früher ja. Heute nicht mehr.
sn.e: She says: it used to be, yes. Not any more.
The third is a yoghurt pot.
A pot has to be clean.

sn.s: Der Becher kommt in den PET-Sack.
sn.e: The pot goes in the PET bag.
The pot is still dirty.
She says nothing.
She just holds it up.

sn.s: Ich sage: Ich muss ihn spülen.
sn.e: I say: I have to rinse it.
She says: exactly.

sn.s: Dann räumt sie alles wieder ein.
sn.e: Then she puts everything back.

sn.s: Sie erklärt mir alles noch einmal.
sn.e: She explains it all to me again.

sn.s: Sie erklärt es langsam und ohne Ärger.
sn.e: She explains it slowly and without irritation.
She is not annoyed.
She really is not annoyed.

sn.s: Aber sie macht sich die Mühe.
sn.e: But she takes the trouble.

sn.s: Sie kommt mit meinem Sack an meine Tür.
sn.e: She comes to my door with my bag.

sn.s: Sie macht ihn auf und schaut hinein.
sn.e: She opens it and looks inside.

sn.s: Und dann erklärt sie mir zwanzig Minuten lang das Trennen.
sn.e: And then she explains separating to me for twenty minutes.

sn.s: Zu Hause ist das sehr komisch.
sn.e: At home that is very strange.
Here it is something else.
I am slowly noticing that.

sn.s: Sie sagt mir nicht: Sie machen es falsch.
sn.e: She does not say to me: you are doing it wrong.

sn.s: Sie sagt: So geht es richtig.
sn.e: She says: this is how it works.

sn.s: Das ist ein kleiner Unterschied und ein grosser.
sn.e: That is a small difference and a big one.
She does not want to tell me off.
She wants to teach it to me.

sn.s: Am Ende sagt sie noch etwas.
sn.e: At the end she says something else.

sn.s: Sie sagt: Bei uns ist das wichtig.
sn.e: She says: with us that is important.
With us.

sn.s: Sie sagt bei uns und sie meint auch mich.
sn.e: She says with us and she means me too.
I hear that at once.
She goes back out.
I rinse every pot.
Rinsing takes ten seconds.

sn.s: Ohne spülen riecht der ganze Sack.
sn.e: Without rinsing the whole bag smells.

sn.s: Ich schaue bei jeder Flasche unten nach.
sn.e: I check the bottom of every bottle.
I leave every lid on.

sn.s: Es dauert zehn Minuten mehr in der Woche.
sn.e: It takes ten minutes more a week.
That is all it is.
In the evening there is another knock.

sn.s: Vor der Tür steht keine Frau Amrein.
sn.e: Frau Amrein is not outside the door.

sn.s: Vor der Tür steht ein Topf.
sn.e: There is a pot outside the door.
There is soup in the pot.
The soup is warm.
It is still completely warm.
I take the pot inside.

sn.s: Ich esse die Suppe am Tisch.
sn.e: I eat the soup at the table.
It is very good.
It is barley soup with bacon.
It tastes of this country.

sn.s: Am nächsten Tag bringe ich den Topf zurück.
sn.e: The next day I bring the pot back.
The pot is clean.
I rinse it twice.

sn.s: Ich sage: Die Suppe ist sehr gut. Merci vielmal.
sn.e: I say: the soup was very good. Merci vielmal.

sn.s: Sie nimmt den Topf und schaut hinein.
sn.e: She takes the pot and looks inside.

sn.s: Sie sagt nichts über die Suppe.
sn.e: She says nothing about the soup.

sn.s: Sie sagt: Der Topf ist sauber.
sn.e: She says: the pot is clean.

sn.s: Von ihr ist das ein Kompliment.
sn.e: From her that is a compliment.
I understand that now.

sn.s: Erst der Sack, dann die Suppe.
sn.e: First the bag, then the soup.

sn.s: Zuerst zeigt sie mir den Fehler.
sn.e: First she shows me the mistake.

sn.s: Dann stellt sie einen Topf vor die Tür.
sn.e: Then she puts a pot outside the door.
Both are the same thing.
Both mean: you belong here.

sn.s: Man sagt es nur nicht so.
sn.e: You just do not say it that way.

sn.s: Man macht den Sack auf und man kocht eine Suppe.
sn.e: You open the bag and you cook a soup.

lessons.title: Ein Monat
lessons.desc: You come home, and the word you use for it is home

sn.s: Ich wohne jetzt einen Monat hier.
sn.e: I have been living here a month now.
A month is not long.

sn.s: Aber es ist genug für vieles.
sn.e: But it is enough for a lot.
It is winter.
The winter here is dark.

sn.s: Um halb fünf ist es dunkel.
sn.e: At half past four it is dark.

sn.s: Um acht Uhr am Morgen ist es noch dunkel.
sn.e: At eight in the morning it is still dark.
In between it is grey.

sn.s: Die Berge sieht man oft nicht.
sn.e: You often cannot see the mountains.
They are behind the clouds.
Sometimes for three weeks.

sn.s: Und dann ist plötzlich alles klar.
sn.e: And then suddenly everything is clear.
Then you can see them again.
And everybody talks about it.

sn.s: Am Abend gehe ich nach Hause.
sn.e: In the evening I go home.

sn.s: Ich gehe den gleichen Weg wie immer.
sn.e: I take the same way as always.

sn.s: Über den Platz, an der Post vorbei.
sn.e: Across the square, past the post office.

sn.s: Dann links und dann die Strasse hinauf.
sn.e: Then left and then up the street.
I do not have to think any more.

sn.s: Ich muss den Weg nicht mehr suchen.
sn.e: I do not have to look for the way any more.
That is a small thing.

sn.s: Aber im ersten Monat ist es keine kleine Sache.
sn.e: But in the first month it is not a small thing.

sn.s: Am Anfang suche ich jeden Weg.
sn.e: At the start I look for every route.
Now I just walk.

sn.s: Im Haus mache ich das Licht an.
sn.e: In the building I switch on the light.

sn.s: Das Licht im Treppenhaus geht nach zwei Minuten aus.
sn.e: The stairwell light goes out after two minutes.

sn.s: Am Anfang bin ich immer im Dunkeln.
sn.e: At the start I am always left in the dark.
Now I walk faster.

sn.s: Ich kenne jetzt viele kleine Sachen.
sn.e: I know a lot of small things now.

sn.s: Ich kenne die Zeiten vom Laden.
sn.e: I know the shop hours.

sn.s: Ich kenne den Fahrplan vom Bus.
sn.e: I know the bus timetable.

sn.s: Ich kenne die Farben von den Containern.
sn.e: I know the colours of the containers.

sn.s: Ich kenne meinen Tag in der Waschküche.
sn.e: I know my day in the laundry room.
That is not German.

sn.s: Aber ohne das kann man hier nicht wohnen.
sn.e: But without it you cannot live here.
My German is better too.
Not much better. But better.
I can read a bill.
I can fill in a form.

sn.s: Ich kann in der Apotheke auf den Hals zeigen.
sn.e: I can point at my throat in the pharmacy.

sn.s: Ich kann mit Frau Amrein reden.
sn.e: I can talk to Frau Amrein.

sn.s: Nicht über alles. Aber über den Tag.
sn.e: Not about everything. But about the day.
I still make a lot of mistakes.

sn.s: Ich sage oft den falschen Artikel.
sn.e: I often say the wrong article.
But I talk.

sn.s: Nuno sagt: Das ist der ganze Trick.
sn.e: Nuno says: that is the whole trick.

sn.s: Man muss reden und Fehler machen.
sn.e: You have to talk and make mistakes.
Otherwise it takes eighteen years.
I am getting used to a lot of things.

sn.s: Sich gewöhnen heisst: es ist nicht mehr komisch.
sn.e: Getting used to it means: it is not odd any more.

sn.s: Ich gewöhne mich an die Stille am Abend.
sn.e: I am getting used to the quiet in the evening.

sn.s: Ich gewöhne mich an den Sonntag ohne Läden.
sn.e: I am getting used to Sunday with no shops.

sn.s: Ich gewöhne mich an die Preise.
sn.e: I am getting used to the prices.
That takes the longest.

sn.s: Ich gewöhne mich an das Grüezi bei jeder Tür.
sn.e: I am getting used to the Grüezi at every door.

sn.s: Am ersten Tag kann ich es nicht sagen.
sn.e: On the first day I cannot say it.

sn.s: Jetzt sage ich es ohne denken.
sn.e: Now I say it without thinking.

sn.s: Am Abend sitze ich am Tisch.
sn.e: In the evening I sit at the table.
The table from the Brockenhaus.
The chair from Frau Amrein.
The ugly yellow lamp.

sn.s: Der rote Teppich für Herrn Bucher.
sn.e: The red rug for Herr Bucher.

sn.s: Jedes Ding hier hat eine Geschichte von einem Monat.
sn.e: Every thing here has a month's story behind it.

sn.s: Das Zimmer ist immer noch fast leer.
sn.e: The room is still nearly empty.

sn.s: Aber es ist nicht mehr das gleiche leere Zimmer.
sn.e: But it is not the same empty room any more.

sn.s: Draussen fängt es an zu schneien.
sn.e: Outside it starts to snow.

sn.s: Der erste Schnee unten in der Stadt.
sn.e: The first snow down in the town.
It does not settle.
But it falls.

sn.s: Ich stehe am Fenster und schaue zu.
sn.e: I stand at the window and watch.

sn.s: Im Haus gegenüber gehen die Lichter an.
sn.e: In the building opposite the lights come on.

sn.s: In jedem Fenster ein anderes Licht.
sn.e: A different light in each window.

sn.s: Um zehn gehen die meisten wieder aus.
sn.e: At ten most of them go out again.
Then it is quiet.
I know this quiet now.

sn.s: Am ersten Abend ist sie zu gross.
sn.e: On the first evening it is too big.

sn.s: Jetzt ist sie einfach der Abend.
sn.e: Now it is simply the evening.
I switch off the light.
I go to bed.
Tomorrow is Thursday.
On Thursday I may do laundry.

sn.s: Ich muss mich in den Plan eintragen.
sn.e: I have to sign myself into the rota.

sn.s: Und ich brauche zwei Franken für den Tumbler.
sn.e: And I need two francs for the Tumbler.
That is what I think in bed.
Not: what am I doing here?

sn.s: Sondern: zwei Franken für den Tumbler.
sn.e: But: two francs for the Tumbler.
In the morning I go down.

sn.s: Frau Amrein steht vor ihrer Tür.
sn.e: Frau Amrein is standing outside her door.
She says Grüezi.
I say Grüezi.
In the evening I come back.

sn.s: Ich mache die Tür auf und ziehe die Schuhe aus.
sn.e: I open the door and take my shoes off.

sn.s: Ich sage nicht: Ich bin in der Wohnung.
sn.e: I do not say: I am in the flat.

sn.s: Ich denke: Ich bin zu Hause.
sn.e: I think: I am home.
The word comes on its own.
I only notice it afterwards.

Warm, and more than a stranger on a pavement was asking for. She will answer you.
Hoi is for people you know. To a stranger it lands as too familiar rather than friendly.

steps.speaker: Die Frau in der Bäckerei
steps.es: Grüezi. Was möchten Sie?
steps.en: Grüezi. What would you like?

options.feedback: Greeting first, then what you want. That order is not optional here.
She greeted you and you went straight to the order. It is not rude, it is just a bit bare.

options.es: Ich möchte ein Brot und ein Gipfeli und zwei Weggli und Käse.
options.en: I would like a loaf and a Gipfeli and two Weggli and cheese.
options.feedback: No Grüezi at all, and all of it at once. Greet, then order, then add.

steps.speaker: Die Frau in der Bäckerei
steps.es: Merci vielmal. Ade.
steps.en: Thanks very much. Goodbye.

options.feedback: You take the leaving word she offered and hand it back. Two syllables and you are out of the door correctly.
Both correct German and both a little German German. Merci and Ade are what you hear in Luzern.
You will hear it, mostly from younger people, and to a woman behind a counter in Luzern it is the wrong register.

scenarios.title: Am Automaten
scenarios.desc: A ticket, a track and eight minutes
scenarios.setting: Zurich airport, underground, with a suitcase and no idea where track seven is.

steps.speaker: Der Automat
steps.es: Wohin möchten Sie fahren?
steps.en: Where would you like to travel to?

options.feedback: Nach for a town or a country. Short is right, it is a machine.
It works. Nach Luzern is the whole answer.
Zu goes to people and to buildings. Towns and countries take nach.

steps.speaker: Ein Mann am Automaten
steps.es: Entschuldigung, sind Sie fertig?
steps.en: Excuse me, are you finished?

options.en: Yes, I am finished. Go ahead.
options.feedback: Bitte on its own is the whole of "go ahead". It does a great deal of work in this language.
Honest and fine if you are not. He will wait.
True, possibly, but bare. Einen Moment costs you nothing.

steps.speaker: Eine Frau am Perron
steps.es: Grüezi. Suchen Sie etwas?
steps.en: Grüezi. Are you looking for something?

options.es: Ja, wo ist Gleis sieben, bitte?
options.en: Yes, where is track seven, please?
options.feedback: Gleis is the numbered track. She will point, or she will walk you there.

options.es: Wo ist der Zug nach Luzern?
options.en: Where is the train to Luzern?
options.feedback: She will understand and answer with a track number, which is what you needed anyway.
Bahnsteig is the German German word. Here it is the Perron, and the number on the board is the Gleis.

steps.speaker: Die Frau am Perron
steps.es: Dort unten, dann rechts. Sie haben noch vier Minuten.
steps.en: Down there, then right. You have four minutes left.

options.feedback: She gave you directions and a warning. Merci vielmal is the right size of thank you for both.
Fine. She did rather more than a plain merci.

options.es: Vier Minuten? Das ist zu wenig!
options.en: Four minutes? That is not enough!
options.feedback: Here four minutes is four minutes. She has told you it is enough by telling you the number.

scenarios.title: Ein Crème, bitte
scenarios.desc: Ordering the coffee, and the word for it
scenarios.setting: The café on the square. Lea is behind the counter and it is not busy.

steps.speaker: Lea
steps.es: Grüezi. Was darf es sein?
steps.en: Grüezi. What can I get you?

options.feedback: Exactly what you said on your first day, and it works. She will ask you which kind.
The Swiss standard coffee, ordered by its name. This is what you learn on day two.
No greeting and no bitte. She will still bring it and she will still notice.

steps.speaker: Lea
steps.es: Einen Crème? Oder eine Schale?
steps.en: A crème? Or a Schale?

options.feedback: You did not know the second word and you picked the one you did know. That is the right move every time.
Asking is not a failure. She will tell you, and you will own the word by tomorrow.
She asked which, not whether. You will get whichever she guesses.

steps.speaker: Lea
steps.es: Möchten Sie auch etwas essen?
steps.en: Would you like something to eat as well?

options.feedback: Nein merci is softer than nein on its own, and it is what people actually say.
Coffee and a Gipfeli is the whole Swiss breakfast and nobody will find it odd at three in the afternoon either.
Understood, and a little flat. Merci does the softening.

steps.speaker: Lea
steps.es: Das macht vier Franken fünfzig.
steps.en: That is four francs fifty.

options.en: (put down four fifty) There you go.
options.feedback: The exact money, so she does not have to give you anything back. Bitte covers the handing over.

options.en: (hand over a twenty) There you go.
options.feedback: Perfectly normal. She will count your change out loud.

options.en: (hand over a two hundred) There you go.
options.feedback: For a four-franc coffee. She will take it, and she will look at you first.

scenarios.title: In der Bäckerei
scenarios.desc: Pointing at things until you have their names
scenarios.setting: Half past six in the morning. Everything is out and nothing is labelled.

steps.speaker: Die Verkäuferin
steps.es: Grüezi. Was möchten Sie?
steps.en: Grüezi. What would you like?

options.es: Grüezi. (auf etwas zeigen) Was ist das, bitte?
options.en: Grüezi. (point at something) What is that, please?
options.feedback: Pointing is not cheating. It is how you get the word, and you only need it once per thing.
You know the word already. No article needed with a number.
She will hand it over. A Grüezi in front of it costs one syllable.

steps.speaker: Die Verkäuferin
steps.es: Das ist ein Gipfeli. Möchten Sie eines?
steps.en: That is a Gipfeli. Would you like one?

options.feedback: You take the word she just gave you and use it in the same breath. That is how it sticks.
Also right, and now you have one for the walk and one for later.
She will know exactly what you mean. She has just told you what it is called here, and you used the other word anyway.

steps.speaker: Die Verkäuferin
steps.es: Sonst noch etwas?
steps.en: Anything else?

options.feedback: She asked an open question and you answered it. This is the point where you add the thing you nearly forgot.
Das ist alles closes the order cleanly.
Fine, if a little short. Nein merci is what she said to you.

steps.speaker: Die Verkäuferin
steps.es: Möchten Sie einen Sack?
steps.en: Would you like a bag?

options.feedback: Fine, and it costs a few Rappen. Most people here have one in their pocket already.
The answer of somebody who has been here more than a week.
Tüte is the German German word. In Switzerland it is a Sack, and it is not free.

scenarios.title: An der Kasse
scenarios.setting: The Migros till on a Friday. Three people behind you and it moves fast.

steps.speaker: Die Frau an der Kasse
steps.es: Grüezi. Haben Sie eine Cumulus-Karte?
steps.en: Grüezi. Do you have a Cumulus card?

options.feedback: You have no idea what it is and it does not matter. Nein merci is a complete answer.
A fair question with nobody behind you. On a Friday evening she will answer it fast.
She will wait for you to produce it, and you do not have one.

steps.speaker: Die Frau an der Kasse
steps.es: Das macht neunundzwanzig Franken fünfundneunzig.
steps.en: That comes to twenty-nine ninety-five.

options.en: (hand over thirty francs) There you go.
options.feedback: Five Rappen back and everybody moves on. This is what the .95 is for.
Nobody will sigh at you. They will all watch, though.
Perfectly normal if you did not catch it. She will say the number again, slower.

steps.speaker: Die Frau an der Kasse
steps.es: Fünf Rappen zurück. Möchten Sie den Bon?
steps.en: Five Rappen back. Would you like the receipt?

options.feedback: Two words and you are done. She is already scanning the next person.
Nothing wrong with it at all.
It is nothing, and it is also her till balancing at the end of the day.

steps.speaker: Die Frau an der Kasse
steps.es: Merci vielmal. Schönen Abend.
steps.en: Thanks very much. Have a good evening.

options.feedback: Gleichfalls is the one word that gives a good-wish straight back, and it works for every one of them.
Completely fine and what most people say.
She wished you something. Two syllables would have covered it.

scenarios.title: Wo ist die Post?
scenarios.desc: Asking, and understanding half the answer
scenarios.setting: You have been walking in circles for ten minutes and every street looks the same.

steps.speaker: Eine Frau auf dem Platz
steps.es: Grüezi.
steps.en: Grüezi.

options.es: Grüezi. Entschuldigung, wo ist die Post?
options.en: Grüezi. Excuse me, where is the post office?
options.feedback: Greeting, apology, question. Three beats and you have not wasted a second of her time.

options.en: Grüezi. I am looking for the post office.
options.feedback: A statement rather than a question, and it works just as well.
She will help you anyway. One word thrown at a stranger is not how it is done here.

steps.speaker: Die Frau
steps.es: Da vorne links, dann geradeaus, und dann noch einmal rechts.
steps.en: Up ahead on the left, then straight on, and then right again.

options.feedback: Repeating it back is how you find out whether you got it, and it takes two seconds.
Asking again is not embarrassing. Walking twenty minutes the wrong way is.
You did not get it and you have just told her you did. You will be back here in five minutes.

steps.speaker: Die Frau
steps.es: Kommen Sie, ich gehe mit. Es ist nicht weit.
steps.en: Come on, I will come with you. It is not far.

options.es: Merci vielmal. Das ist sehr freundlich.
options.en: Thanks very much. That is very kind.
options.feedback: Accept it. This is the normal answer here and refusing makes it awkward for both of you.
She will let you go. She was not being polite, she genuinely finds it easier than explaining.

options.en: No. I will find it myself.
options.feedback: Flat, and she was doing you a kindness. Nein, nein, das geht schon does the same job without the edge.

steps.speaker: Die Frau
steps.es: So, das gelbe Haus dort. Das ist die Post.
steps.en: There, the yellow building there. That is the post office.

options.feedback: She walked five minutes out of her way. Merci vielmal, not merci.

options.es: Gelb. Das merke ich mir. Merci.
options.en: Yellow. I will remember that. Merci.
options.feedback: And you should. The post office is yellow in every town in the country.
A little thin for somebody who escorted you there.

scenarios.title: Am Brunnen
scenarios.desc: The water is free and somebody will tell you
scenarios.setting: A hot afternoon on the square, with a two-franc bottle of water in your hand.

steps.speaker: Eine alte Frau
steps.es: Grüezi. Haben Sie Durst?
steps.en: Grüezi. Are you thirsty?

options.feedback: She is going somewhere with this. Answer and let her get there.

options.es: Grüezi. Ja, es ist warm heute.
options.en: Grüezi. Yes, it is warm today.
options.feedback: The weather, offered back. That is how a conversation starts here.
She greeted you first. One word back leaves the greeting hanging.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Sie müssen das Wasser nicht kaufen. Dort ist ein Brunnen.
steps.en: You do not have to buy water. There is a fountain over there.

options.feedback: The obvious question, and asking it is how you stop buying water for good.
She has just saved you two francs a day. Take it.

options.es: Das Wasser im Brunnen? Nein, merci.
options.en: The water in the fountain? No, thanks.
options.feedback: She is not offering you puddle water. Almost every fountain in the country runs drinking water.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Natürlich. Fast alle Brunnen sind Trinkwasser.
steps.en: Of course. Almost all the fountains are drinking water.

options.feedback: Exactly the right follow-up. There is a sign, and it says kein Trinkwasser.
Go and fill the bottle you already paid for. That is the whole trick.

options.es: In der Stadt? Das ist nicht sauber.
options.en: In town? That is not clean.
options.feedback: It comes off the mountain and it is colder and cleaner than the bottle in your hand.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Das macht jeder am Anfang. Ade.
steps.en: Everybody does that at the start. Goodbye.

options.feedback: She told you something useful and did not make you feel stupid. That deserves the full merci vielmal.
Correct, and it skips the thank you she had earned.

options.en: I am not at the start.
options.feedback: You are, and she was being kind about it.

scenarios.title: Am Samstagabend
scenarios.desc: The shop shut two hours ago
scenarios.setting: Half past six on a Saturday, no milk in the flat, and everything dark.

steps.speaker: Ein Mann vor dem Laden
steps.es: Der ist schon zu. Seit fünf.
steps.en: It has been shut since five.

options.feedback: Say the thing you cannot believe. He will explain it, because everybody here has had this conversation.
Fine, and it ends the conversation before he tells you the useful part.

options.es: Aber es ist erst halb sieben.
options.en: But it is only half past six.
options.feedback: It is, and the shop shut at five regardless. Arguing with the opening hours is a beginner move.

steps.speaker: Der Mann
steps.es: Am Samstag schliessen die Läden früh. Und am Sonntag ist alles zu.
steps.en: On Saturday the shops close early. And on Sunday everything is shut.

options.feedback: Yes. This is the single most useful fact anybody will tell you in your first month.
Sometimes it opens for an hour or two in the morning. That is the whole exception, apart from the station.

options.es: Das ist nicht gut für den Laden.
options.en: That is not good for the shop.
options.feedback: Everybody here has decided otherwise, repeatedly, at the ballot box.

steps.speaker: Der Mann
steps.es: Am Bahnhof ist etwas offen. Auch am Sonntag.
steps.en: There is something open at the station. On Sunday too.

options.en: At the station? Thanks very much!
options.feedback: The station shops are the exception the whole country runs on. Now you know it too.
Yes. And it is open, which on a Sunday is the only thing that matters.
It is a fifteen minute walk and the alternative is no milk until Monday.

steps.speaker: Der Mann
steps.es: Nächstes Mal am Freitag einkaufen. Ade.
steps.en: Do your shopping on Friday next time. Goodbye.

options.en: Thanks. I will do that. Goodbye.
options.feedback: You will, and by the third weekend it will not be a decision any more.
He gave you the rule and the exception in under a minute. Worth the vielmal.
He stopped in the street to save you a wasted Sunday.

scenarios.title: Die Schlüsselübergabe
scenarios.desc: Three keys and a great deal of information
scenarios.setting: Two o’clock, an empty flat, and a landlord who says everything twice.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Grüezi. Also, das ist die Wohnung.
steps.en: Grüezi. So, this is the flat.

options.feedback: His name back to him. Nobody here minds being called by it, and using it says you were listening.
Fine. Merci is the word you will hear back from him.
It is empty because it was handed over cleaned to the corner, which is what he is about to explain.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Der erste Schlüssel ist für die Wohnung, der zweite für das Haus.
steps.en: The first key is for the flat, the second for the building.

options.feedback: There is always a third and it is always the cellar. Asking is quicker than being told twice.
He will say it again anyway. He says everything twice.
You do. The cellar is where your bike is going to live.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Nach dem Duschen müssen Sie das Fenster aufmachen. Sonst gibt es Schimmel.
steps.en: After showering you have to open the window. Otherwise you get mould.

options.feedback: Short and it is a promise. Mould at the handover comes out of your deposit.
Especially in winter. Asking shows you took it as a rule and not as small talk.
He will let that pass and he will remember it.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Die Miete müssen Sie bis am dritten bezahlen. Nicht am vierten.
steps.en: You have to pay the rent by the third. Not the fourth.

options.es: Bis am dritten. Ich schreibe es auf.
options.en: By the third. I will write it down.
options.feedback: He said a date and a not-date. Repeating the date back is the whole answer.
True, and it does not show him you registered which day.
Then a Mahnung comes, it costs twenty francs, and you have just told your landlord you might.

scenarios.title: Am Dienstag gewaschen
scenarios.desc: You used the machine on somebody else’s day
scenarios.setting: The laundry room, two hours later, with your washing still in the machine.

steps.speaker: Frau Steiner
steps.es: Entschuldigung. Der Dienstag ist mein Tag.
steps.en: Excuse me. Tuesday is my day.

options.feedback: She is right, and saying so ends it. Nobody here wants an argument, they want the rota kept.

options.es: Die Maschine ist leer. Ich dachte, es geht.
options.en: The machine was empty. I thought it was fine.
options.feedback: A reason, which she will accept and not agree with. Empty is not the same as free.

options.en: But nobody is using it right now.
options.feedback: That is the argument, and it is the one that makes an enemy in a building you will live in for years.

steps.speaker: Frau Steiner
steps.es: Sie müssen sich in den Plan eintragen. Dann gehört der Tag Ihnen.
steps.en: You have to sign into the rota. Then the day is yours.

options.es: Ich trage mich das nächste Mal ein.
options.en: I will sign myself in next time.
options.feedback: Uses her own verb back. eintragen is the word the whole system runs on.
On the wall by the door. Asking is better than guessing again.
Yes, and it is in the Hausordnung, which she knows and now knows you have not read.

steps.speaker: Frau Steiner
steps.es: Nehmen Sie Ihre Wäsche heraus. Ich brauche die Maschine jetzt.
steps.en: Take your washing out. I need the machine now.

options.feedback: Immediate and one more apology. That closes it properly.
The Tumbler is Tuesday’s too. You are asking for the second half of the day you already took.
Reasonable, and she has been waiting two hours already.

steps.speaker: Frau Amrein
steps.es: Und? War die Frau Steiner böse?
steps.en: Well? Was Frau Steiner cross?

options.feedback: The right answer, and she will report it to the building exactly as you said it.
Honest. She will tell you Frau Steiner is never cross, which is nearly true.

options.en: How do you know about it already?
options.feedback: She always knows already. Asking her that is a joke she will enjoy.

scenarios.title: Beim Hauswart
scenarios.desc: Reporting a problem, in the one hour he is there
scenarios.setting: Five o’clock, the ground floor, and a bathroom light that stopped working yesterday.

steps.speaker: Ruedi Zemp
steps.es: Grüezi.
steps.en: Grüezi.

options.es: Grüezi. Das Licht im Bad ist kaputt.
options.en: Grüezi. The bathroom light is broken.
options.feedback: Greeting and then the problem in one short sentence. He is waiting for exactly that and nothing else.

options.en: Grüezi. Do you have a moment?
options.feedback: Polite, and it makes him ask what for. He would rather you just said it.
Not unfriendly, just not what this hour is for. He will wait for the actual reason.

steps.speaker: Ruedi Zemp
steps.es: Welche Wohnung?
steps.en: Which flat?

options.feedback: Two words. He is already writing it in the book.

options.en: The flat next to Frau Amrein.
options.feedback: He knows exactly which one that is. The number is faster.

options.es: Ich wohne seit einem Monat hier.
options.en: I have been living here a month.
options.feedback: Not the question. He asked which flat.

steps.speaker: Ruedi Zemp
steps.es: Morgen um acht.
steps.en: Tomorrow at eight.

options.feedback: He will be there at eight. Not five past. Take the time and say thank you.
It could, and you have just made work out of something that was finished.

options.es: Können Sie es heute noch machen?
options.en: Could you still do it today?
options.feedback: You report a problem to him. You do not set his schedule.

steps.speaker: Ruedi Zemp
steps.es: So. Das Licht geht wieder.
steps.en: There. The light works again.

options.en: Thanks very much. That was quick.
options.feedback: Four minutes. Noticing it out loud is the closest thing to a compliment he will accept.
Fine. He will nod and pack up.
He will tell you in about six words. It is a fair question.

scenarios.title: Bei der Gemeinde
scenarios.setting: Eight in the morning, ticket B twelve, and a folder with four documents in it.

steps.speaker: Der Beamte
steps.es: Grüezi. Was kann ich für Sie tun?
steps.en: Grüezi. What can I do for you?

options.en: Grüezi. I would like to register.
options.feedback: The exact sentence for the exact counter. He will have the form out before you finish it.
True, and he still has to ask what you want. anmelden is the word.

options.en: Grüezi. I need a bank account.
options.feedback: Wrong building. But you do need this first, and the bank will ask for what he is about to give you.

steps.speaker: Der Beamte
steps.es: Haben Sie einen Ausweis?
steps.en: Do you have ID?

options.feedback: bitte handing something over is one of the four jobs that word does.
It is. Asking costs nothing.
Then this is a second trip. Bring everything, every time.

steps.speaker: Der Beamte
steps.es: Und die Religion? Sie müssen das nicht ausfüllen.
steps.en: And religion? You do not have to fill that in.

options.feedback: Because the church is funded by tax here. He will tell you plainly and it is worth knowing.

options.en: Then I will leave it empty.
options.feedback: He told you it was optional. Taking him at his word is fine.

options.en: Do I have to fill that in?
options.feedback: He has just said you do not. Worth listening to the second half of the sentence.

steps.speaker: Der Beamte
steps.es: So. Das ist die Bestätigung. Willkommen in Luzern.
steps.en: There. That is your confirmation. Welcome to Luzern.

options.feedback: He meant the welcome. It is said without ceremony and it is not nothing.
For the bank and for the insurer. Do not lose it, which is what he is about to say.
It is. Eleven minutes, which will keep surprising you.

scenarios.title: Der Nachbar an der Tür
scenarios.desc: He came up two floors in his socks
scenarios.setting: Three in the afternoon. You have just dragged a table across a wooden floor twice.

steps.speaker: Herr Bucher
steps.es: Grüezi. Ich bin Bucher, von unten.
steps.en: Grüezi. I am Bucher, from downstairs.

options.feedback: You know why he is here and you say so first. That is the whole conversation over in one line.

options.es: Grüezi. Was kann ich für Sie tun?
options.en: Grüezi. What can I do for you?
options.feedback: Polite, and it makes him say the awkward part out loud.

options.es: Grüezi. Es ist erst drei Uhr.
options.en: Grüezi. It is only three o’clock.
options.feedback: It is, and he works at home, which he has not told you yet because you did not let him.

steps.speaker: Herr Bucher
steps.es: Ich arbeite unten.
steps.en: I work downstairs.

options.en: I did not know that. Sorry.
options.feedback: He is not complaining, he is telling you a fact you needed. Take it that way.

options.en: I will not move anything else.
options.feedback: Concrete, and it is the thing he actually wants.
Yes. And now you know why the building is silent at eleven in the morning.

steps.speaker: Herr Bucher
steps.es: Haben Sie einen Teppich?
steps.en: Do you have a rug?

options.es: Nein. Aber ich kann einen kaufen.
options.en: No. But I can buy one.
options.feedback: That is the answer he came up two floors for, and he did not have to ask for it.
It does, a lot, and asking makes it his suggestion rather than your concession.
He would not have mentioned it otherwise.

steps.speaker: Herr Bucher
steps.es: Grüezi. Wie geht es?
steps.en: Grüezi. How are you?

options.es: Grüezi, Herr Bucher. Gut, merci. Und Ihnen?
options.en: Grüezi, Herr Bucher. Good, thanks. And you?
options.feedback: Two weeks and a rug later, he is asking. That is not a small thing here — answer it properly and ask back.
Correct and it leaves his question half answered. The Und Ihnen is the other half.
The everyday answer, and it lands as easy rather than formal. He will use it back at you.

scenarios.title: Bei Nuno
scenarios.desc: Friday at seven, and he does come at seven
scenarios.setting: A kitchen after service, a bottle of something, and the first person here who talks fast.

steps.speaker: Nuno
steps.es: Hoi! Komm rein.
steps.en: Hi! Come in.

options.feedback: Hoi back, not Grüezi. He offered du and the informal greeting in one word, and taking it is the answer.
Not wrong, and it is a step more formal than what he just gave you. He will not mind and he will notice.
The other informal one. Same register, and it is what you would hear around Zurich and the centre.

steps.speaker: Nuno
steps.es: Und? Wie ist der erste Monat?
steps.en: Well? How is the first month?

options.feedback: Two words and he will laugh, because it is exactly right and he remembers it.
Honest, and it opens the conversation he wants to have.
True, and it is the thing every newcomer says first. He has heard it eighteen years running.

steps.speaker: Nuno
steps.es: Lern die Artikel jetzt. Sofort. Nicht später.
steps.en: Learn the articles now. Straight away. Not later.

options.es: Der Tisch, die Wohnung, das Bad.
options.en: Der Tisch, die Wohnung, das Bad.
options.feedback: You did not agree, you demonstrated. That is the only answer he wanted.
They do. And everybody hears it, which is what he is trying to tell you.
This is the one piece of advice he gives everybody, because nobody gave it to him.

steps.speaker: Nuno
steps.es: Die Fehler sind nicht das Problem. Das Schweigen ist das Problem.
steps.en: The mistakes are not the problem. The silence is the problem.

options.feedback: You do. Forty minutes at an airport without saying a word taught you the same thing.

options.es: Zwei Jahre still. Das ist lang.
options.en: Two years silent. That is a long time.
options.feedback: It is, and he said it about himself. Repeating it back shows you heard which part mattered.

options.es: Ich habe keine Angst vor Fehlern.
options.en: I am not afraid of mistakes.
options.feedback: Everybody says that in the first month. He will simply keep talking to you and find out.

kennen.en: to know a person or place

phrases.en: I only speak a little German.

phrases.es: Bitte langsam. Ich verstehe nicht alles.
phrases.en: Slowly, please. I do not understand everything.
